summary: Verified new admin Approvals section + Promoters (referral rewards) UI end-to-end on the preview URL, plus backend contract via pytest (14/14 passing). Approvals section loads, all 5 category sub-tabs render live data (restaurants=1, drivers=157, car_rentals=1, businesses=5, users=53). Toggle expands a full-detail grid, Orders button opens the order-history-dialog (drivers first record shows order-history-empty as expected). Users category correctly hides approve/reject buttons and detail grid contains no hashed_password/password/session_token strings. Promoters tab shows all 3 summary cards (pending_first_order/held/paid) and the Referral Rewards ledger (admin-referral-rewards). Backend pytest confirms: (a) GET /api/admin/records/{category} returns 200 with count+records+full for all 5 categories, 403 for non-admin, 401/403 unauth, 404 for unknown category; (b) GET /api/admin/records/{category}/{id}/orders returns type='order' for drivers and type='rental' for car_rentals, 403 for non-admin; (c) sensitive fields scrubbed from users records; (d) GET /api/admin/promo-rewards returns {rewards, counts:{pending_first_order,held,paid}, currency, reward_schedule}. First-order settlement logic remains covered by pre-existing test_first_order_reward.py.

issues: Console warning: Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby` for DialogContent. Add a DialogDescription (or aria-describedby) for accessibility compliance.

action_items: (Minor a11y) Add DialogDescription/aria-describedby to the order-history-dialog and other Radix DialogContent uses to silence the accessibility warning.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py has grown to ~10.5k lines - please prioritize splitting into route modules (admin, orders, payments, drivers, promoters). Continuing to add features in one file will make regressions increasingly hard to catch.

GET /api/admin/records/{category} intentionally exposes the full document minus MongoDB _id (and sensitive fields for users). Consider a stricter allowlist per-category (e.g. never return raw tokens/OTP hashes/webhook secrets if any are ever added to other collections) rather than a denylist that only covers users.
AdminApprovals.js renders potentially 157 driver rows in a single flat list without virtualization. On slower devices this could jank; consider paginating or virtualizing when count > ~50.
